record_notes.DCP-LETT-1865: Before May 3, 1856 fragment, source preserved under older period; all six surviving blocks, five notes and annotations freshly reread after prior accepted note. No bibliography section. Opening and end missing. Surviving pigeon statements are limited-range beliefs and uniform coloration, with general conjugal-fidelity qualification; the particular cock entering a domestic dovecot is absent from surviving portion. P5 explicitly answers drifted-tree query, P4 offers help. These match 1867 independently of editorial dating. Raw XML lower1809 is indexing bound, not plausible exact composition evidence; correspondent identified from Darwin note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1867: May 3, supplied 1856; all five blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Acknowledges missing-from-fragment cock-pigeon case in P1, but P3 first sentence uniquely answers surviving 1865 driftwood report. P2 takes up explicit assistance offer with specimen and second-head request, postage conditional. P4 answers personal biography question missing from fragment. Later book evidence of actual specimens not backdated. Editorial summary mentions rabbit query but none occurs in this surviving body; do not import it into answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1954: September 11, supplied 1856; six blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Earlier Shetland specimen now examined; requests another for previously omitted eyelid/crop points, ideally early winter. Chequered plumage and domestication questions still unanswered; salt-preserved rabbit sought without head damage, Porto Santo specimen already received. This proves specimen custody, not arrival of Wollaston cover. Edmondston fatherhood learned from missing letter some two months earlier, approximate not exact July day. Later rabbit table not current result.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2079: April 19, supplied 1857; three blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Pigeons physically received a few days earlier with scrap promising fuller letter; that cover missing, no exact arrival day. Further pigeon specimens unnecessary, rabbit still pending. Graba and Colonel King reports distinct; King cannot recall original plumage twenty years earlier. Raw repeated near Hythe preserved. Body Hebrides differs from later quoted Variation Orkney provenance; no silent harmonisation. 1954 is Darwin request, not incoming response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2131: August 2, supplied 1857; seven blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing letter of July23 and rabbit, encloses postage reimbursement. Declines live young pigeons because insufficient prospective generations, not a failed completed experiment. Dun/mouse/cream/roan/chestnut stripes, foal prominence, ancestry and inheritance are queries with explicit doubts and mixed observation/hearsay. Norway letter sent, answer not thereby present. Later book not evidence of Shetland findings.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2021F: December 24, supplied 1856; five blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Complete three-page outgoing despite F suffix. Question distinguishes dioecious/monoecious/close hermaphrodite structures and actual versus apparent fertilisation; Knight occasional-crossing idea under investigation, not proved universal law. Hooker referral is Joseph Dalton per apparatus, despite summary W. J. Hooker. Safe return and Oxford memory not exact dates of scientific evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2035: January 3, 1857; six blocks, five notes, separate annotations, bibliography and actual image independently read. Darwin letter delivered during Harvey absence, personally received evening January3; do not equate earlier address delivery with personal access, or either with Darwin receipt. Describes known algae mostly monoecious, near-adjacent sexes, exceptions with separate cysts and several dioecious genera; Floridean double-female terminology retained historically, qualified male inference. No known true floral hermaphroditism stated with nearest examples. P1 diagram viewed in original context: open-topped rounded receptacle with larger outlined bodies and clusters of dark short strokes, illustrating juxtaposition; unlabeled and not a quantitative tally or species diagnosis. Thuret paper recommendation not proof of Darwin reading. Dublin invitation answered in 2037G; undated chapter3 annotation separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2037G: January 7, supplied 1857; both blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Thanks just desired amount of information and declines likely Dublin visit because sea sickness. Specific invitation in2035 plus substantive response identifies direct reply. Later nonattendance in apparatus not an observed January event; no exact incoming arrival given.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1026F: November17,1856 copy, not autograph; five blocks and two notes read, no bibliography. Tenant drainage/building history reported; Higgins earlier refusal as agent separate from present proposed compensation. Upcoming rent audit November25. Says three modes but surviving text sets out payment with five-percent interest or diminishing fifteen-year lien; do not invent a third option. Annual reduction is genuine MathML1/15 followed by superscript th, not integer115. £43.10.0 increase is pounds/shillings/pence, not decimal pounds. Proposed arrangements, not executed lease; later answer uniquely chooses second.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1993: November19, supplied1856; three blocks, three notes read, no bibliography. Acknowledges increased rent and prefers fifteen-year lien for £105, but permits Higgins advice favoring payment with five-percent interest if fairer tenant treatment. Can send money immediately is conditional, not executed transfer or unqualified binding acceptance. Later December19 account credit not known as completed here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2181F: December9,1857 exact; all three retained blocks, excluded supplemental signature, note and bibliography read. Acknowledges £248:2:1 bank credit; historical pounds/shillings/pence not decimal amount. Ch. Darwin across receipt stamp is excluded supplemental autograph layer, while body valediction remains. Receipt duty described in apparatus contextualizes stamp, not research instruction. No incoming account text survives, so no synthetic prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1834: February29, supplied1856 leap year; all seven blocks, twelve notes and bibliography read. Requests permission to combine Berkeley seed results, natural-family order and plant identities. Plans further flotation trial because prior plants kept warm/dark may have decayed too fast; distinguish plants floating from seed germination. Pea observations have immature harvest and separation limitations. Mere variation versus direct pollen action unresolved; Gärtner and nursery practices seem conflicting, not settled conclusion. Offers Vilmorin samples; later self-fertilisation explanation belongs apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1836: March7,1856 damaged ALS; six blocks, eight notes, annotations and bibliography read. Grants seed-results use and recommends Lindley order; Corn salad species uncertain, aubergine Solanum Melongena and dwarf Belgian Phaseolus vulgaris identified. Pea colour changes may be mere variation, cannot decide with one or two experiments or attribute changes to neighbour pollen. Lacks Gärtner book. Busy cryptogamic book, Rawson question, request black peas, and isolated red seeds yielding mottled seed separately retained. Long P1 has several topics, not merely pea response. Darwin Vibrio note undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1843A: March18, supplied1856; three blocks and three full notes read, no bibliography section. Explicit thanks March7 permission, now sent paper to Linnean Society. Sending black/intensely purple-pod peas answers request. Dispatch is not recipient receipt, March manuscript submission not May6 public reading or later journal publication. Complete short ALS despite letter suffix.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1078: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Only an editorial synopsis of a ten-page algae memorandum is transcribed; no Darwin wording survives on this page. Assigned April 7, 1847 inferred from Hooker forwarding reference with explicit on-or-around caveat, not exact memo composition/dispatch. Underlying Beagle diary notes and missing specimens are described but not reproduced. Published Harvey account or Darwin Coral reefs cannot substitute for full memorandum. Record fully inspected, authentic body unavailable.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1566: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 9, supplied 1854. Considers switching fourteen thousand pounds into guaranteed railway shares because prices have fallen, with a hypothetical nearly-five-percent return and depreciation reserve. Unnamed relative advice is distinct from Higgins advice. Asks whether a farm survey incurred costs and says he encloses five guineas for prior help; later July 8 account entry is not April settlement evidence. Farm purchase remains a fallback if railway prices rise before July. These are his historical expectations, not guaranteed realised returns.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1594: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October 5, supplied 1854. A missing Higgins letter and plan offer a nearby estate, but Darwin declines because money is now invested, much for seven years. Explicitly reports following Higgins suggestion by Great Northern mortgage and B shares. This is completed-investment evidence by October 5, unlike March/April plans. Detailed July transaction dates, amounts and 4 1/4-percent rate are quoted later from the investment book; keep their source and chronology separate. No surviving covering offer or plan is identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1615: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Christmas Day 1854. Acknowledges missing note/account and net credit 217 pounds 16 shillings 8 pence. Gross account figure differs by fifteen-shilling Agricultural Club payment. Wishes Higgins family well and reports two sons improving after fever and inflammation; their identities and later diary interval are editorial evidence, not all events known on Christmas. The original receipt and forthcoming calendar dates stay distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1687: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 26, 1855. Short acknowledgement of half-year rent 212 pounds 6 shillings 5 pence and good farm report. The incoming report/account is unlocated. Earlier 1854 Christmas credit and July 1852 rent argument cannot substitute for this missing prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1662: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 7, supplied 1855. Seven blocks, eleven footnotes and bibliography. Darwin saw peas at Kew under misleading labels; his then belief in Berkeley pollen-affected specimens preserved without importing later correction. Forty-one reputed varieties planned in two or three days, white Sugar Pea received today instead of desired brown type. Requests dozen brown peas and unplanned extended Gärtner fertility interpretation, including table versus text tensions and possibly biased seed counts. Reading straight through underway; June rereading and October completed abstract later. Berkeley abstract known, not preserved incoming letter. Proposed correspondence with Gärtner does not imply he was alive; apparatus states death 1850. Undated annotations and later October note separately dated. Category labels retained as transcribed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1665: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 11, supplied 1855. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Curious pea gift received by writing, all kinds new except Queen of Dwarfs; exact arrival not specified. French preservation of giant variety supposed through grouping, not proved practice. Follow-up information conditional; silence would be interpreted as lack of knowledge, not actual negative answer. Gärtner opinion inquiry referred back to 1662; neither outgoing letter becomes incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1699: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 12, supplied 1855. Six blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Missing Berkeley note reports salting experiments; printed approbation distinct source. Wants five-day interval clarified as wet or partly dry; later report omission and Darwin later counting it are apparatus, not current answer. Today accidental drying of eight/ten-week and dried seed series feared lethal, not established germination result. Some seeds actually germinated after 56 days, late germination observed; Hooker interest but little/no persuasion is Darwin assessment. Berkeley peas up; publication and correspondence not merged.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1710: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 3, supplied 1855. Sixteen extracted blocks and footnote; complete raw HTML inspected. Soaking results span species rows and continuing condition phrases: Beet/Rhubarb 65 days cold, Orache 82 cold, Oats/Canary/Capsicum 70 ordinary temperature, Cress/Lettuce/Radish/Carrott 70 with few and delayed germination, Celery/Onion 85. Raw HTML contains only successive paragraphs and no table or retained braces/column structure; this interpretation cannot silently become exact source prose. Layout rendering hold, preserve sequence and ambiguity pending authoritative witness. Peas growing, distinct from initial receipt. No missing incoming prompt required for volunteered progress report.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Rounded open-topped receptacle containing larger outlined oval/circular bodies and clusters of dark strokes. Inserted directly in Harvey discussion of male/female structures within a common receptacle. Schematic, no labels or scale; no count or taxon identification inferred solely from drawing.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
